title: Generation and functional characterization of murine mammary organoids
protocol: Euthanize one mouse at a time using laboratory standard procedures and as approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
Spray the ventral side of the mouse with 70% ethanol and rub against the hair to ensure thorough cleaning.
Transfer the mouse into a biosafety cabinet.
Place the mouse on a clean tray, and tape/pin the feet to expose the ventral side up.
Cut one ventral midline from the inguinal nipples towards the thoracic nipples along the skin without cutting the peritoneum.
Make two lateral incisions from the central midline towards each side of the mouse flanks.
Lift and peel the skin to expose the inguinal (4th and 5th pairs) mammary fat pads.
Locate the lymph nodes within the mammary fat pads and use a pair of forceps to squeeze and remove them.
Cut and remove the inguinal fat pads from each side of the mouse flank using clean scissors and tweezers.
Place the removed fat pads in a 100 mm tissue culture dish containing 5 ml of basal DMEM/F12 medium with 5% FBS, at room temperature.
Autoclave dissecting tools or submerge in 100% ethanol for 30 minutes before use.
Maintain mammary fat pads at 20°C–25°C in DMEM/F12 medium with 5% FBS while collecting samples.
Hold mammary fat pads with tweezers and dip each into a conical tube containing fresh PBS-1× to rinse off hairs and blood.
Place two pairs of fat pads from the same mouse on a fresh 100 mm dish.
Mince the glands using a sterile razor blade, holding it vertically and performing perpendicular cuts by alternating vertical and horizontal cuts.
Mince two pairs of fat pads at a time for 3 minutes to obtain a homogeneous tissue mixture with minimal cellular damage.
Transfer minced tissue from the same mouse into a 50 mL tube containing 10 mL of Digestion medium I.
Shake the tube at 200 rpm in a 37°C orbital shaker for 40 minutes.
At the end of the digestion, vortex the tube for 5 seconds at medium speed.
Transfer the content into a clean 15 mL tube.
Pre-warm Digestion medium I in a 37°C water bath.
Digest 4 mammary fat pads from one mouse using 10 mL of pre-warmed Digestion medium I.
Centrifuge the mixture at 450 × g for 10 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant, including the fat layer, into a new collecting tube and set aside.
Resuspend the tissue pellet in fresh basal DMEM/F12 medium (plus 5% FBS) to stop enzymatic digestion.
Close the lid and invert the tube a few times to mix the solution.
Transfer 1 mL of tissue suspension into a well of a 24-well plate.
Observe the digested tissue under a bright field microscope.
Verify that at least hundreds of fragments have been isolated after digestion I.
Transfer the 1 mL suspension of mammary fragments from the 24-well back into the centrifuge tube.
Combine with the remaining 4 mL of suspension.
Rinse the wells with 1 mL of basal DMEM/F12 medium (+5% FBS).
Combine the rinse solution with the 5 mL from step g.
Centrifuge the tube at 450 × g for 5 min if RBC are present.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Tap and flick the tube to dislodge the tissue pellet and expose any red blood cells.
Add 2 mL of RBC lysis buffer and incubate for 1 min at 20°C–25°C if RBC are present.
Add 8 mL of PBS-1× (+1% FBS) to dilute the RBC lysis buffer and pipet up and down a few times.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 1 min after adding PBS-1×.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Add 2 mL of TrypLE and digest the pellet containing fragments for 5 min in a 37°C waterbath.
Add 6 mL of PBS-1× (+1% FBS) to stop the enzymatic reactions, close the lid and invert the tube 3–4 times.
Spin at 450 × g for 5 min after adding PBS-1× to stop enzymatic reactions.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend the pellet with 2 mL of Digestion medium II.
Place the tube in a 37°C waterbath for 5 min.
Tap and invert the tube during incubation steps as needed for cell dissociation.
Add 6 mL of 0.1% FBS in PBS and invert the tube 3-4 times.
Centrifuge the sample at 450 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of organoid culture medium.
Pipette 20 μL of aggregates suspension into a well containing 20 μL of trypan blue.
Count the numbers of cell aggregates using a hemocytometer.
Progressively reduce the concentration of FBS from 5% to 0.1% when resuspending cell pellets.
Resuspend cell pellet at 1 × 10^6 cells per 100 μL of FACS buffer (1% FBS in PBS-1×).
Incubate the suspension at 20°C–25°C for 20 min with diluted fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies directed at lineage markers: CD31, CD45, TER119, EpCAM and CD49f.
Wash cells twice with 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Centrifuge the samples at 500 × g for 3 min.
Resuspend each cell pellet in 200 μL of FACS buffer containing 1 μg/mL DAPI.
Stain cells with EpCAM and CD49f to distinguish luminal and basal epithelial cell populations.
Gate for P1 to isolate epithelial cells, excluding stromal cells.
Count sorted luminal and basal cells.
Plate the counted cells in Matrigel domes.
Allow organoids to grow for 18 days in culture.
Identify three types of organoid colonies: solid colonies, cystic colonies with bright reflection, and budding colonies with protruding cells.
Culture mammary epithelial cells in Matrigel for approximately one week before passaging.
Thaw Matrigel in a 4°C cold room for 14–16 hours or on ice at 20°C–25°C for 1–2 hours.
Wet pipette tips with pre-chilled PBS-1×.
Mix the Matrigel solution by pipetting up and down 4–5 times before use.
Pipette 10 μL of Matrigel in the center of each well to form a flat layer of ∼1 cm in diameter.
Transfer the wells to a 37°C cell incubator for 10 minutes.
For each well of a 24-well plate, pipette a volume of cell suspension containing 30,000 cell aggregates.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube containing 9 times the volume of Matrigel.
Mix the cell suspension and Matrigel thoroughly in the centrifuge tube.
Dispense the mixture in each pre-coated well to generate a Matrigel dome of appropriate size (e.g., 50 μL for 30,000 cells).
Plate additional wells by preparing a master suspension with increased volume of cell suspension multiplied by the number of intended wells plus one extra well.
Transfer the cell suspension into a centrifuge tube containing nine times the volume of Matrigel and mix thoroughly.
Keep tubes containing Matrigel on ice until plating.
Take the pre-coated 24-well plate from the incubator and place it in the tissue culture hood.
Pipette and mix the cell aggregates/Matrigel suspension before plating.
Position the pipette vertically over the center of a well and pipette the Matrigel containing cells in the middle to form a small dome.
Gently transfer the 24-well plate to a 37°C cell incubator for 30 min to allow Matrigel to set.
Take the 24-well plate back to the hood.
Gently overlay 1 mL of pre-warmed Organoid culture medium in each well.
Return the plate to the 37°C cell incubator.
Change culture medium every 2 days.
Avoid touching or disturbing the cell dome while pipetting the medium off.
Carefully add 1 mL of pre-warmed fresh medium.
Process mice as in Step 2.
Dissect out mammary tumors, place them in a 100 mm dish and remove normal-looking mammary fat pads.
Process one sample at a time using a razor blade to cut tumors into small portions and mince until it reaches a consistent texture.
Incubate minced tumor tissue in 10 mL of Digestion medium I for one hour in a 37°C orbital shaker at 200 rpm.
Centrifuge to collect cell pellet and rinse it once in 5 mL of DMEM/F12 + 5% FBS.
Collect the pellet and follow Step 4.k to remove RBC if present.
Digest each sample containing tumor fragments with 3 mL of TrypLE first, followed by a digestion with 3 mL of Digestion medium II sequentially.
Resuspend each cell pellet in 5 mL of Organoid culture medium.
Count the tumor fragments following step 4.u.
Plate 30,000 cell aggregates in a 50 μL Matrigel dome.
Overlay the dome with 1 mL of Organoid culture medium.
Culture and passage as described in step 7.
Passage organoids when more than 70% of colonies reach approximately 200 μm in size.
Dilute organoids at a ratio of 1:4 to 1:6 for re-plating.
Thaw fresh aliquots of Matrigel on ice in a cold room for 14–16 hours or at 20°C–25°C for 1–2 hours.
Aspirate the culture medium without touching the cell dome using a vacuum aspirator.
Add 1 ml of TrypLE to each confluent well and gently break the Matrigel by pipetting up and down 5-6 times.
Incubate the 24-well plate at 37°C in a cell incubator for 2 min.
Place the plate in the tissue culture hood after removal from the incubator.
Mechanically dissociate mammary organoids into smaller aggregates by pipetting several times to assist enzymatic digestion.
Return the plate to the incubator for another 3 min of digestion.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 15 ml tube at the end of the digestion.
Add 3 ml of 0.1% FBS in basal DMEM/F12 medium to stop TrypLE action.
Centrifuge the tubes at 450 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of Organoid culture medium.
Count the number of cell aggregates.
Transfer 30,000 cell aggregates in Organoid culture medium to a 1.5 mL tube containing 9 volumes of Matrigel.
Plate the dome of cell aggregates in the middle of a well in a fresh 24-well plate.
Pre-coat the wells with Matrigel before plating.
Prepare organoid freezing medium by making up a solution of 90% FBS and 10% DMSO, at room temperature.
Set a cryopreservation container filled with propan-2-ol aside, at 20°C–25°C.
Gently aspirate the medium off the 24-well plates containing confluent organoids.
Dissociate organoids into cell aggregates as per steps 7.a to 7.g.
Centrifuge the dissociated organoids.
Resuspend each cell pellet in 0.5 mL of freezing medium.
Transfer resuspended cells into a cryovial.
Place the cryopreservation container with cryovials into a −80°C freezer.
Transfer cryovials into a liquid nitrogen tank for long-term storage after 24 hours.
Thaw fresh aliquots of Matrigel on ice in a 4°C cold room for 14–16 hours, or on ice at 20°C-25°C for 1–2 hours.
Warm the Organoid culture medium in a 37°C water bath for 10 minutes.
Place the cryovial containing frozen organoids in a 37°C water bath for 2–3 minutes, or until almost fully thawed.
Transfer 0.5 mL of organoids in freezing medium into a 15 mL tube.
Add 5 mL of basal DMEM/F12 medium to the tube.
Centrifuge at 450 × g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant, leaving a layer of basal DMEM/F12 medium to cover the pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet in a solution containing 1 part Organoid culture medium and 9 parts Matrigel.
Plate between 50 and 100 μL of organoids/Matrigel mixture per well.
Plate content from one cryovial into three wells.
Treat mammary organoid lines with various PI3K and AKT inhibitors at different concentrations the day after plating.
Refresh drug solutions every two days for 4 days of treatment.
Process growth rate of treated mammary organoids using the Promega CellTiter – Glo 3D assay.
Pre-coat each of the required wells of a 96-well plate with 5 μL of Matrigel.
Incubate the plate in a 37°C incubator for 5 min.
Leave the plate in the cell culture hood at room temperature after 5 min incubation.
Avoid plating cells in the outer wells when using 96-well plates to circumvent the “edge effect” and evaporation of culturing medium.
Fill the empty wells with 200 μL of sterilised water to minimize loss of volume in experimental wells.
Count the number of cell aggregates in a 24-well plate containing organoid cultures.
Prepare a cell/Matrigel suspension with a concentration of 8000 cell aggregates per 20 μL total volume.
Transfer 20 μL of cell/Matrigel mixture into each well of a 96-well plate using a P-20 tip.
Gently and slowly pipette the 20 μL of cell/Matrigel suspension right at the center of the well, on top of the Matrigel coating layer.
Leave the 96-well plate at 37°C in a cell incubator to set for 20 min.
Once the Matrigel has set, take the 96-well plate back to the hood and overlay 200 μL of Organoid culture medium per well.
Incubate the 96-well plate at 37°C in a cell incubator for 6 days.
Refresh Organoid culture medium every 2 days.
Measure growth of organoid colonies using a CellTiter-Glo 3D assay.
Optional: The day after plating, gently aspirate 200 μL of Organoid culture medium from the well without disturbing the cell dome.
Prepare a master mix containing the drug concentration to be tested diluted in Organoid culture medium.
Include additional wells treated with vehicles as controls.
Pipette the Organoid culture medium off and add 200 μL of master mix to each well of a 96-well plate.
Incubate the 96-well plate at 37°C in a cell incubator for 4 days.
Note: Treatment can be refreshed every 2 days.
At the end of the experiment, measure growth of organoid colonies using a CellTiter-Glo 3D assay.
Treat additional well of organoids with 0.1% Triton X-100 diluted in Organoid culture medium for 1 min before staining as positive control.
Stain the positive control and experimental samples simultaneously with propidium iodide (PI) and Hoechst 33342.
Replace the Organoid culture medium with 200 μL of staining medium.
Place the organoids in a 37°C cell incubator and let them stain for 30 min.
Remove the staining medium without disturbing the cell dome.
Add 200 μL of PBS-1× to the organoids.
Measure the fluorescent PI signal using a multi-mode microplate reader (e.g., CLARIOstar PLUS microplate reader).
Adjust focal height.
Measure fluorescence signals using excitation and emission wavelengths for PI: 535 nm and 617 nm.
Measure fluorescence signals using excitation and emission wavelengths for Hoechst 33342: 361 nm and 486 nm.
Measure the PI signal first.
Measure the Hoechst 33342 signal next.
Cultivate wild-type mammary organoids in Organoid culture medium.
Supplement the medium with increasing concentrations of noggin conditioned medium.
Incubate for 6 days.
Assay effect on cell death using propidium iodide (PI) and Hoechst33342 stain.
Use wells treated with 0.1% Triton-X 100 in Organoid culture medium as positive control.
